_comment: Statement boundary data for the five migrations whose `statements` arrays in
supabase_migrations.schema_migrations hold MORE THAN ONE element.
Background: Supabase stores an applied migration either as one element (the
whole file, executed through the simple query protocol) or as an array of
individual statements split on top-level `;` terminators. Where it split, the
terminator itself was consumed, so array_to_string(statements, E'\n') - the
fidelity oracle used to recover these files byte-exactly - yields SQL with NO
top-level semicolons, i.e. text that no PostgreSQL client can execute.
This file records, per version, the byte length of each statement as stored.
Because the joined text is exactly statements joined by a single '\n', the end
offset of statement i is  sum(len[0..i]) + i.  make_executable.py re-inserts a
';' at each of those offsets, restoring the terminators the splitter removed.
SELECT length(x)::text FROM unnest(statements) AS x), ',')
Invariant asserted by make_executable.py:  sum(lens) + (n - 1) == len(joined).
